title: Unique extension along the concrete diagonal unit
statement: Let X be a scheme and A a functor from etale set sheaves on X to pro-etale set sheaves on X. Suppose e_F,Y identifies A(F)(Y) with terminal sections of the etale inverse image Y.hom^*F, naturally in coefficient maps, and intertwines restriction along each Z to Y with the inverse-image unit along that arrow followed by inverse terminal transport [def-weil-pbc-sets-terminal-transport]. let eta be the explicit natural transformation of [def-cbc-comparison-section-diagonal-unit]. For every etale set sheaf F and pro-etale set sheaf G, the map sending beta:A(F) to G to eta_F followed by the restriction of beta is bijective. Equivalently every morphism F to the etale restriction of G has exactly one extension beta with that fixed diagonal restriction. The assertion concerns this specified map, not the existence of a hom-set equivalence or an adjunction.

source.place: Tag 0GLZ, diagonal unit and sectionwise transpose argument; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GLZ (read online; local source absent)

proof.text: Restrict G to the etale site over each weakly etale Y by the composite of Scheme.toProEt Y.left and MorphismProperty.Over.map for Y.hom. Their existing continuity instances make this a sheaf. Restrict alpha_U to Y times_X U, transpose using the etale inverse-image adjunction and evaluate at Y to construct beta_Y.

The composition-unit equality proves naturality under Z to Y using hres. On etale U, the inverse-image/restriction unit formula identifies beta on the specified diagonal section with alpha_U, proving surjectivity.

For any extension beta, its components on etale V over Y decode to a morphism Y.hom inverse image F to G restricted to Y_et. Naturality at Y times_X U to U and the diagonal formula fix its adjoint transpose. Injectivity of the etale adjunction hom equivalence identifies it with the constructed transpose. Evaluation at Y proves uniqueness and hence injectivity.

theorem proEtaleComparisonSectionUnit_bijective (X : Scheme.{u})
    (A : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)) ⥤
      Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (Type (u + 1)))
    (e : ∀ (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) (Y : X.ProEt),
      (A.obj F).obj.obj (op Y) ≃
        ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback Y.hom).obj F).obj.obj
          (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.left))))
    (hres : ∀ (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
      (Y Z : X.ProEt) (g : Z ⟶ Y) (s : (A.obj F).obj.obj (op Y)),
      e F Z ((A.obj F).obj.map g.op s) =
        (((Functor.sheafPullbackConstruction.sheafAdjunctionContinuous
            (MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @Etale ⊤ g.left) (Type (u + 1))
            (Y.left.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)
            (Z.left.smallGrothendieckTopology @Etale)).unit.app
              ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback Y.hom).obj F)).hom.app
                (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.left))) ≫
            (etaleSetTerminalTransport Y.hom g.left Z.hom g.w F).inv) (e F Y s))
    (hfun : ∀ (F F' : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1))) (ψ : F ⟶ F')
      (Y : X.ProEt) (s : (A.obj F).obj.obj (op Y)),
      e F' Y ((A.map ψ).hom.app (op Y) s) =
        ((Scheme.etaleSetPullback Y.hom).map ψ).hom.app
          (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 Y.left))) (e F Y s))
    (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (Type (u + 1)))
    (G : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) (Type (u + 1))) :
    Function.Bijective (fun f : A.obj F ⟶ G ↦
      (proEtaleComparisonSectionUnit X A e hres hfun).app F ≫
        ((Scheme.toProEt X).sheafPushforwardContinuous
          (Type (u + 1)) X.smallEtaleTopology (Scheme.ProEt.topology X)).map f)
